newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA PROTEST OVER TEST PITCH-SWITCH.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA PROTEST OVER TEST PITCH-SWITCH.

text.p: Australian tour manager Alan Crompton has made an official complaint about the pitch-switch for the fourth Ashes test at Headingley, he said as play started on Thursday.
With less than five overs possible before mid-afternoon on the first day because of rain, the cricket was overshadowed by the continuing pitch row.
The Australians were angry that England chairman of selectors David Graveney may have been involved in the decision in an attempt to negate the strengths of their leg-spinner Shane Warne.

Crompton said: "It is totally inappropriate for the chairman of selectors to have anything to do with the choice of pitch and preparation of the pitch, and of all things the late decision to change the pitch.
"Australia's only concern is the identity of the person who took the decision to change pitches."
He said he had spoken to Tim Lamb, chief executive of the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB), on Wednesday evening and planned to do so again later on Thursday.

Australian captain Mark Taylor said he was "disappointed" by the change from the proposed pitch to an adjoining one, which he felt should not have been done only a few days before the match. He said the new strip was "under-prepared".
But an ECB spokesman said the decision had been made as long ago as last Wednesday by director of pitches Harry Brind.
The strip originally chosen apparantly had bare patches with little grass cover.
There has been a running debate throughout the series about whether pitches should be tailored to suit the home side.
Taylor claimed that at a recent meeting of all test captains it was agreed that preparation should be left to the groundsman, without interference.
"They should cut out the best wicket they see fit," he said.
